newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Burns Philp to sell herb/spice unit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Burns Philp to sell herb/spice unit.

text.p: Food ingredients group Burns Philp and Co Ltd said on Monday it would sell its United States-based herb and spice business, allowing it to focus on its yeast operations.

The company, which has suffered lower profits over the last two years and restructured its operations a number of times, said the latest operational review was conducted in conjunction with The Boston Consulting Group. The review included a study of the amount of time and resources required to generate adequate returns from the herb and spice businesses and the growth opportunities in yeast and related products.

"Burns Philp intends to sell its consumer spice and industrial food service operations in North America and Europe to focus on the company's global yeast business. No changes are planned for the company's investments division," it said.

The company said Barings had been given the mandate to sell the North American and European herb and spice businesses, which consist of Durkee-French, Spice Islands, Tone's, British Pepper and Spice, Euroma and Ostmann. It said the businesses may be sold separately on a geographic basis or to one buyer.

"A number of the world's largest food companies have previously expressed interest in acquiring some or all of these businesses," the company said. It said the sales process could take up to six months.
The restructuring of Burns Philp into the Yeast/Bakery, Industrial/Food Service and Consumer divisions took effect in July last year.
Yeast/Bakery had sales of A$357.1 million in the 1996/97 first half ended December 31 and earnings before interest and tax of A$34.6 million.
Consumer foods had pre-tax earnings of A$38.1 million on sales of A$352.2 million, while Industrial/Food Service had sales of A$230.4 million and earnings of A$12.3 million.
